    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-24680\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Kapoor\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Lin\",\n  \"project\": \"Console Rollouts\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-01\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"a/b\",\n    \"auto-rollback\",\n    \"tracing\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"PM-14091\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-20345\",\n    \"ENG-20412\",\n    \"DES-317\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"console-2026.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window\",\n    \"Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals\",\n    \"User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)\",\n    \"Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation\",\n    \"Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model\",\n    \"All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV\",\n    \"Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta\"\n  ],\n  \"tasks\": [\n    \"Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)\",\n    \"Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap\",\n    \"Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison\",\n    \"Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests\",\n    \"Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins\",\n    \"SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics\",\n    \"QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios\",\n    \"Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook\"\n  ],\n  \"design_assets\": [\n    \"https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype\",\n    \"https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_queries\": [\n    \"PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\\\"/v1/generate.*\\\"}[5m]) by (cohort)\",\n    \"PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))\",\n    \"SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)\",\n    \"Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)\",\n    \"GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)\"\n  ],\n  \"risks\": [\n    \"High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow\",\n    \"Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes\",\n    \"Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust\",\n    \"Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis\"\n  ],\n  \"tradeoffs\": [\n    \"Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \\u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas\",\n    \"Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially\",\n    \"Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle\"\n  ],\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Nina Rodriguez (Security)\",\n    \"Omar Patel (SRE)\",\n    \"Leah Chen (Design)\",\n    \"Devon Morris (Engineering lead)\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action\",\n    \"Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate\",\n    \"Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 Aisha       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-24680-cohort-comparator-and-trace-linker-for-deployment-health.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: product-management\nProject: Console Rollouts\nTeam: product-management\n\n- comparator ui shows side - by - side cohort - level charts for latency ( p50 / p95 ), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window - diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals - user can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request - level metadata ( route, model version, routing policy, input hash ) - trace linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors ( e. g., model variant, batch size, region ) derived from instrumentation - auto - rollback triggers are visible per - rollout and can be toggled ; console records the reason and suggested fallback model - all",

document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-24680",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "creator": "Aisha Kapoor",
  "assignee": "Marco Lin",
  "project": "Console Rollouts",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-04-01",
  "labels": [
    "rollouts",
    "observability",
    "console",
    "canary",
    "a/b",
    "auto-rollback",
    "tracing"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-14091"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-20345",
    "ENG-20412",
    "DES-317"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2026.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window",
    "Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals",
    "User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)",
    "Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation",
    "Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model",
    "All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV",
    "Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    "Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)",
    "Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap",
    "Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison",
    "Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests",
    "Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins",
    "SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics",
    "QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios",
    "Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook"
  ],
  "design_assets": [
    "https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype",
    "https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf"
  ],
  "telemetry_queries": [
    "PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m]) by (cohort)",
    "PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))",
    "SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)",
    "Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)",
    "GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow",
    "Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes",
    "Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust",
    "Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis"
  ],
  "tradeoffs": [
    "Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas",
    "Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially",
    "Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Nina Rodriguez (Security)",
    "Omar Patel (SRE)",
    "Leah Chen (Design)",
    "Devon Morris (Engineering lead)"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action",
    "Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate",
    "Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket \u2014 goal is to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions by surface-level correlation -> request-level evidence.",
    "2026-03-11 Marco Lin: Spun up spike; backend will reuse existing metrics pipeline but needs a lightweight join index for cohort -> trace linking (ENG-20345)",
    "2026-03-12 Leah Chen: Uploaded first mockups; recommended adding a confidence ribbon to diff charts to indicate statistical significance",
    "2026-03-13 Omar Patel: SRE flagged potential retention cost issue; recommending adaptive sampling and a 14-day lookback default",
    "2026-03-14 Marco Lin: Marked 'in progress' \u2014 backend API contract drafted and PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128"
  ],
  "attachments": [
    "https://confluence.redwood/internal/Console-Rollouts/Cohort-Comparator-PRD",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/ab12cd34",
    "https://internal.redwood/incidents/2025-11-canary-regression-postmortem.pdf"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "tasks",
    "rollout_plan",
    "risks",
    "tradeoffs",
    "notes",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_54525a33e2d44d4a9b665feaf8fab624"
}

    "title": "Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"134876\",\n  \"title\": \"Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Khan\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-28\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/sdk-cross-adapter-token-provider\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Ethan Walsh\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez\",\n    \"Jordan Lee\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"auth\",\n    \"ergonomics\",\n    \"chore\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4026\",\n    \"ENG-4041\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"12\",\n  \"additions\": \"842\",\n  \"deletions\": \"210\",\n  \"description\": \"This PR introduces a language-agnostic stream-adapter registry and a pluggable token-provider abstraction to the SDK surface so that each SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. Motivation: persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across SDKs were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. The change packages three coordinated pieces: 1) a lightweight StreamAdapterRegistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to SDK adapters; 2) a PluggableTokenProvider interface plus a default refresh provider used by hosted and dedicated customers; 3) thin ergonomic wrappers added to each SDK exposing the provider as an opt-in parameter and a compatibility shim for older code paths. Checklist: - [x] Core registry implementation and protocol contract - [x] Default token provider implementation and short-circuit for static tokens - [x] SDK wrappers: python client convenience function, TS builder option, Go functional option - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests for resume/reconnect and single-token refresh paths - [x] Documentation snippets and migration notes - [x] Version bumps for SDK packages (python/ts/go) Compatibility notes: the adapters are opt-in by default; existing call sites continue to work. To enable the new behavior set `stream_adapter: \\\"registry-v1\\\"` and pass `token_provider` in the client constructor. There is an opt-in migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md. Rollout plan: merge to main, cut a patch release for hosted clients who opt-in, coordinate SDK releases in the same week to avoid partial parity. Related work: ENG-4026 (streaming-reconnect stability), ENG-4041 (sdk-auth-resilience).\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"9f2b7a1 - core: add StreamAdapterRegistry and protocol contract\",\n    \"a3d4e02 - auth: introduce PluggableTokenProvider and default refresher\",\n    \"b71c9f3 - sdk/python: expose token_provider param and add thin adapter\",\n    \"c8d20e4 - sdk/typescript: builder option + tests for backpressure semantics\",\n    \"d4f11b5 - sdk/go: functional option + fixes for reconnect double-reauth\",\n    \"e16a332 - tests: cross-sdk integration harness and CI workflow updates\",\n    \"f28b44c - docs: migration guide and example snippets\"\n  ],\n  \"changed_files\": [\n    \"core/streaming/adapter_registry.py\",\n    \"core/auth/token_provider_interface.go\",\n    \"sdk/python/redwood/client.py\",\n    \"sdk/python/tests/test_stream_adapter_integration.py\",\n    \"sdk/typescript/src/stream/builder.ts\",\n    \"sdk/typescript/test/stream/backpressure.spec.ts\",\n    \"sdk/go/options/stream_opt.go\",\n    \"sdk/go/integration/stream_integration_test.go\",\n    \"docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md\",\n    \"ci/workflows/cross-sdk-integration.yml\",\n    \"pkg/versioning/sdk_version_manifest.json\",\n    \"CHANGELOG.md\"\n  ],\n  \"review_thread\": [\n    \"Ethan Walsh: Overall looks good; please add explicit unit tests for the python token refresh race (requester saw double-refresh in prod).\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Added python unit that simulates concurrent KV cache invalidation and verified single refresh path (see new test).\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez: TS builder ergonomics are better but please ensure default builder remains zero-config for existing users.\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Builder defaults preserved; added explicit e2e backpressure test to assert no extra buffering on reconnect.\",\n    \"Jordan Lee: small nit on Go naming and a suggestion to document semantics of the token_provider lifecycle.\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Renamed method to TokenProviderLifecycle() and added documentation block in sdk/go/README.md.\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez: CI flaky test (ts/backpressure) failed once; re-ran and it passed. Approving after green CI.\",\n    \"Ethan Walsh: Approved. Verified integration harness reproduced previous double-reauth; new registry fixes scenario.\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit: python - pass\",\n    \"unit: typescript - pass\",\n    \"unit: go - pass\",\n    \"integration: cross-sdk - pass\",\n    \"lint: python/ts/go - pass\",\n    \"e2e: smoke - pass\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merge_commit\": \"squash-merge 7a3d4f (stream-adapter-registry)\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Added a stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers. SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) now accept an optional token_provider for streaming calls to control refresh lifecycle. Opt-in by default. Bugfix: prevents duplicate token refresh during stream reconnects. SDK version bumps: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v0.9.0.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"no\",\n  \"testing\": [\n    \"Local unit tests for each SDK and core (python/ts/go)\",\n    \"Cross-SDK integration harness that drives connect/resume scenarios with deterministic delays\",\n    \"Load-run smoke test to ensure no regression in streaming throughput\",\n    \"Manual verification with a staging Dedicated cluster to validate token rotation under sustained reconnects\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_thread\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f5b6b65ec24e4e19b81c4e96d35bf77c\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-134876-stream-adapter-pluggable-token-provider-cross-sdk-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: redwood\n\ndescription : this pr introduces a language - agnostic stream - adapter registry and a pluggable token - provider abstraction to the sdk surface so that each sdk ( python / typescript / go ) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. motivation : persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across sdks were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. the change packages three coordinated pieces : 1 ) a lightweight streamadapterregistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to sdk adapters ; 2 ) a pluggabletokenprovider interface plus a default refresh provider used",

{
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "134876",
  "title": "Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps",
  "author": "Aisha Khan",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-28",
  "merged_at": "2026-03-01",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/sdk-cross-adapter-token-provider",
  "reviewers": [
    "Ethan Walsh",
    "Marta L\u00f3pez",
    "Jordan Lee"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "streaming",
    "auth",
    "ergonomics",
    "chore"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4026",
    "ENG-4041"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "12",
  "additions": "842",
  "deletions": "210",
  "description": "This PR introduces a language-agnostic stream-adapter registry and a pluggable token-provider abstraction to the SDK surface so that each SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. Motivation: persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across SDKs were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. The change packages three coordinated pieces: 1) a lightweight StreamAdapterRegistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to SDK adapters; 2) a PluggableTokenProvider interface plus a default refresh provider used by hosted and dedicated customers; 3) thin ergonomic wrappers added to each SDK exposing the provider as an opt-in parameter and a compatibility shim for older code paths. Checklist: - [x] Core registry implementation and protocol contract - [x] Default token provider implementation and short-circuit for static tokens - [x] SDK wrappers: python client convenience function, TS builder option, Go functional option - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests for resume/reconnect and single-token refresh paths - [x] Documentation snippets and migration notes - [x] Version bumps for SDK packages (python/ts/go) Compatibility notes: the adapters are opt-in by default; existing call sites continue to work. To enable the new behavior set `stream_adapter: \"registry-v1\"` and pass `token_provider` in the client constructor. There is an opt-in migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md. Rollout plan: merge to main, cut a patch release for hosted clients who opt-in, coordinate SDK releases in the same week to avoid partial parity. Related work: ENG-4026 (streaming-reconnect stability), ENG-4041 (sdk-auth-resilience).",
  "commits": [
    "9f2b7a1 - core: add StreamAdapterRegistry and protocol contract",
    "a3d4e02 - auth: introduce PluggableTokenProvider and default refresher",
    "b71c9f3 - sdk/python: expose token_provider param and add thin adapter",

document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "gmail-soojin-20260818-hc-exc-001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "laura_bennett",
    "markus_klein",
    "neha_kapoor"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Polaris Talent <sarah@polaris-talent.com>",
    "GreenCore migrations (eng@greencore.com)"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "related_links": [
    "JIRA: INFRA-2247",
    "Drive: https://drive.redwood/workspace/platform/migration-risk-matrix"
  ],
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "hc_exception_form.pdf",
    "migration_risk_matrix.xlsx",
    "cost_breakdown_6mo.csv"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Hi Laura / Markus,

Tl;dr: Requesting a one-time hiring-freeze exception to backfill a departing Senior Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) on Platform Services. This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.

Why this is exceptional:
- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).
- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). Migration has hard deadlines tied to customer contract INFRA-2247.
- Impact: with current staffing we estimate +30–45% risk of missing the rollout milestone and elevated on-call burden across two teams.

Proposed path:
1) Approve HC exception to backfill Senior IC (IC4) with either direct hire or 6-month contractor through Polaris Talent (attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv).
2) If approved, prioritize internal candidates first (we have one internal transfer candidate in org).
3) If approval delayed >7 days, we will request temporary time-limited escalation budget for overtime and hiring agency retained search.

Attached: HC exception form (filled), migration risk matrix, six-month cost comparison (direct hire vs contractor).

Ask: Approve or provide guidance on preferred funnel (internal transfer vs external contractor) by EOD Aug 18 so we can start vendor engagement.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Services
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0142

[attachment: hc_exception_form.pdf] [attachment: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx] [attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv]",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13 11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick Qs before I greenlight:

1) Headcount budget: do you have the hiring cost vs committed budget this FY (include recruiting fees if external)? I saw your attachment but would like a one-line delta to the org budget.
2) Coverage plan: if we approve internal transfer, who covers the gaps left by that transfer? (need names/teams).
3) SLA tolerances: quantify the customer impact in $ or churn risk if migration slips by 4 weeks.

If you can get me the answers and sign-off from Finance (Markus) and HR (Neha) by EOD Aug 18 I can approve the exception. If Finance can't commit, consider a 6-month contractor approval as fallback.

— Laura
VP Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 9:15 AM Soojin Lee wrote:...",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-14 08:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Laura — quick follow with the concrete numbers you asked for:

1) Budget delta: direct hire (mid-band IC4) fully loaded = $240k/yr total comp equivalent; recruiting + ramp = ~ $30k in Y1, so net delta to FY budget = +$270k. 6-month contractor via agency = ~$85k (includes agency fee). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.
2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. Proposed mitigation: shift two noncritical tickets to FY27 backlog and assign a 3rd rotation from SRE for 6 weeks.
3) SLA impact: conservative estimate is $120k ARR at risk (single large customer migration) and increased engineering support cost ~$25k in third-party consulting if we miss milestone by 4 weeks.

Attached is an updated one-pager summarizing these points and the requested approval box filled out on the HC exception form. I recommend approving a contractor for 6 months while we run a parallel external search — this minimizes SLA risk and gives time to evaluate internal transfer without blocking the migration schedule.

If you want, I can arrange a short sync with Finance (Markus) and Neha to run through the numbers tomorrow.

— Soojin

[inline: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx excerpt]

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Sarah Miller <sarah@polaris-talent.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14 07:22 -07:00
Subject: Candidate availability

Soojin — we have two senior infra contractors available starting 9/7 and a permanent candidate who could move by late Sept. If you'd like the contractor hold we'll need a 3-day confirmation.

Best,
Sarah
Polaris Talent",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18 16:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

All — reviewed the cost sheet and migration risk matrix. Finance can support a time-limited contractor approval up to $95k for six months on the condition that: 

- Recruiting runs concurrently and we aim for a permanent hire within 4 months,
- Team documents handover & runbooks in the first 30 days (Soojin, please own),
- A post-mortem and budget reconciliation is provided to Finance within 90 days.

Laura — if that's acceptable from your side, consider this the Finance conditional approval. Neha — please confirm any compliance/contracting constraints on short-term contractor engagements and confirm whether Polaris has passed vendor onboarding.

Markus Klein
Director, Finance Planning
Redwood Inference

  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json",
    "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Martinez\",\n    \"Sara Kim\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"adr\",\n    \"contract-testing\",\n    \"schema-fencing\",\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"conformance\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\",\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary \\\"schema fencing\\\" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.\\n\\nContext and motivation\\n\\nRecent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:\\n\\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\\n\\nThis ADR proposes:\\n\\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\\n2. A \\\"schema fencing\\\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\\n\\nScope\\n\\nApplies to:\\n\\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n\\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\\n\\nKey concepts\\n\\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\\n\\nSchema fencing:\\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\\n\\nConformance matrix and ledger:\\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\\n\\nRules and compatibility classes\\n\\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\\n\\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\\n\\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\\n\\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\\n\\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\\n\\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\\n---\\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\\nscope: public\\nversion: 1.0.0\\nmode: strict\\nrequest: \\n  content-type: application/json\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      prompt:\\n        type: string\\n      features:\\n        type: object\\n        additionalProperties: true\\n    required: [prompt]\\nexamples:\\n  - name: simplest\\n    request: {\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text...\\\"}\\nresponse:\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      id: {type: string}\\n      output: {type: string}\\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\\n    required: [id, output]\\npredicates:\\n  - description: output must be non-empty\\n    jq: \\\".output | length > 0\\\"\\nconformance_category: strict\\n\\nAutomation and CI integration\\n\\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\\n\\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\\n\\nConformance ledger and dashboard\\n\\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\\n\\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\\n\\nOperational SLOs and alerting\\n\\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\\n\\nGating and release policy\\n\\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\\n\\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\\n\\nTelemetry and observability requirements\\n\\nEach contract-test run must emit:\\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\\n- conftest.endpoint\\n- conftest.test_case_id\\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\\n- conftest.duration_ms\\n\\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\\n\\nOwner and stewardship\\n\\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\\n\\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\\n\\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\\n\\nMigration plan\\n\\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\\n\\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\\n\\n# Local validation\\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\\n\\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml\\n\\n# Central conformance run (dry-run example)\\n#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv\\n\\n# Linter rules (excerpt)\\n# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]\\n\\nNotes on documentation style\\n\\n- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.\\n- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.\\n\\nReferences\\n\\n- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\\n- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\\n\\nApproval\\n\\nApproved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290\"\n}",

document.title: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing
document.content:
{
  "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
  "space": "architecture-and-standards",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Martinez",
    "Sara Kim",
    "Liam O'Connor"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "adr",
    "contract-testing",
    "schema-fencing",
    "ci-cd",
    "conformance"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025",
    "/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary "schema fencing" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.

Context and motivation

Recent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:

- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).
- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).
- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.

This ADR proposes:

1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.
2. A "schema fencing" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.
3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.

Scope

Applies to:

- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).
- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).
- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.

Out of scope:

- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.
- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.

Key concepts

Declarative contract test spec (DCTS):
- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).
- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).

Schema fencing:
- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.
- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.

Conformance matrix and ledger:
- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.
- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.

Rules and compatibility classes

Fields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:

- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.
- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.
- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.
- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).

Change proposal workflow (brief)

1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.
2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

Example DCTS snippet (YAML)

# Example: /v1/generate request/response
# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml
---
endpoint: POST /v1/generate
scope: public
version: 1.0.0
mode: strict
request: 
  content-type: application/json
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      prompt:
        type: string
      features:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
    required: [prompt]
examples:
  - name: simplest
    request: {"prompt": "Summarize the following text..."}
response:
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      id: {type: string}
      output: {type: string}
      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}
    required: [id, output]
predicates:
  - description: output must be non-empty
    jq: ".output | length > 0"
conformance_category: strict

Automation and CI integration

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).
- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.

Cross-repo conformance job (central):
- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.
- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)
- conftest.endpoint
- conftest.test_case_id
- conftest.result (pass|fail)
- conftest.duration_ms

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

Appendix: sample CLI commands and linter config

# Local validation
#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml

# Publish artifact (CI step)
#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml

# Central conformance run (dry-run example)
#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv

# Linter rules (excerpt)
# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]

Notes on documentation style

- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.
- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.

References

- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025
- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026

Approval

Approved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-12876\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"stabilization-window-rc-eligibility-orchestrator\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Ruiz\",\n  \"project\": \"release-train-2026\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-15\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"release-engineering\",\n    \"rc-automation\",\n    \"lts\",\n    \"observability\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-31247\",\n    \"ENG-52391\"\n  ],\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Problem: Our current weekly build -> RC tagging flow relies on ad-hoc human checks and a separate release notes generation step. This causes two recurring issues: 1) borderline builds get promoted without a predictable stability gate, increasing hotfix churn on LTS lanes; 2) release notes are assembled manually from PR templates and often miss runtime-impacting changes (batching, KV cache, kernel selection) unless authors explicitly tag them.\\n\\nGoal: Implement a stabilization-window + RC eligibility orchestrator that programmatically evaluates candidate weekly builds across signal tiers (test flakes, canary SLO deltas, perf regressions, eval quality checks) and produces: (a) an explicit RC candidate list with provenance and confidence score; (b) automated RC tagging in git for eligible candidates; (c) automated release notes draft enriched with runtime-impact metadata and links to performance dashboards. The orchestrator should also expose a small human review UI in Console to approve/override candidates before final tagging for the weekly LTS lane.\\n\\nHigh level proposal:\\n- Stabilization window: run a deterministic 48-hour window after each weekly build where the orchestrator aggregates signals and computes an \\\"eligibility_score\\\" per build. Signals include flaky test score (30%), canary SLO delta (30%), per-token latency regression (20%), eval-suite regression rate (15%), and security policy scans (5%).\\n- RC eligibility rules engine: translate score + hard gates into an outcome: eligible/conditional/blocked. Hard gates: critical test failures, policy scan failures, or >2% canary SLO regression => blocked. Conditional builds require human review.\\n- RC tagging automation: for eligible builds, create a lightweight release branch and annotate with metadata (build id, score, signal links), then tag git as rc-{semver}-{date}. If conditional, mark in Console and create a reviewer assignment.\\n- Release notes automation: use PR metadata, label heuristics, and runtime changelog parsers (scan commit messages for keys like BATCHING, KV_CACHE, KERNEL) to synthesize a structured notes draft. Enrich with links to: perf dashboard (grafana), integration test run (CI URL), and eval diff (s3 path). Also include a human-editable summary in Console.\\n\\nNon-goals: full replacement of human judgment for exceptional releases; automatic LTS promotion without explicit approval.\\n\\nTrade-offs considered:\\n- Strict numeric gating vs. fuzzy scoring: chosen hybrid (score + hard gates) to balance automation with engineer oversight.\\n- Time window length: 48h is a compromise between fast weekly cadence and collecting meaningful stability signals. Can be tuned via config.\\n- Complexity of release-note NLP: initial implementation will be rule-based heuristics to keep scope small; later iterations may add ML-based grouping.\\n\\nOperational notes:\\n- The orchestrator will run as a daily job in the release namespace and listen for new weekly build events.\\n- All decisions are recorded in a release provenance log with links to artifacts for audit.\\n- Console feature flags will gate auto-tagging and the human-review UI so we can do staged rollout to internal teams first.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Orchestrator aggregates signals and computes eligibility score for a weekly build within 1 hour of window close\",\n    \"Eligible builds are auto-tagged with RC tags in main git repository when auto-tagging feature flag is enabled\",\n    \"Conditional builds surface in Console with reviewer assignment and a concise provenance panel\",\n    \"Release notes draft is generated for every candidate and includes links to perf dashboard, CI run, and eval diff\",\n    \"All decisions are logged and queryable via the release provenance dashboard\"\n  ],\n  \"tasks\": [\n    \"Design eligibility scoring formula and threshold defaults (owner: Marco)\",\n    \"Implement signal adapters: flaky test score (CI), canary SLO delta (telemetry), perf regression extractor (perf infra)\",\n    \"Build rules engine and mapping to eligible/conditional/blocked outcomes\",\n    \"Implement git tagging flow + metadata annotation service\",\n    \"Create release-notes synthesizer with PR label and commit tag heuristics\",\n    \"Console: small review UI and feature flag for auto-tagging\",\n    \"Add audit log entries to provenance store and wire to existing release dashboard\",\n    \"End-to-end QA run on internal staging with three weekly builds\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"Per discussion with PM (Lina Chen) we must include explicit canary SLO delta links so on-call can trace regressions quickly\",\n    \"Initial score weights were tuned after running the formula over the last 12 weeks of historical builds; see spreadsheet in Confluence\",\n    \"We plan to gate auto-tagging behind 'release.auto_tag' feature flag and enable only for non-LTS lanes initially\",\n    \"Ops request: include an 'escape hatch' playbook that allows immediate manual un-tag + emergency hotfix flow\",\n    \"Security scanning adapter will surface policy failures but not block RC tagging until we complete remediation workflow (follow-up ticket)\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELEASE/pages/RC+Eligibility+Orchestrator\",\n    \"Design doc draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/rc-eligibility-design\",\n    \"Perf dashboard (example): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/perf/weekly-builds?orgId=1\",\n    \"CI flaky score job: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/flaky-score\",\n    \"GitHub PR for prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/412\",\n    \"Release provenance dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/releases/provenance\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-02 Marco Ruiz: Initial spike completed. Scored last 12 weekly builds locally \\u2014 score correlates with post-release hotfix count (r=0.68). Moving to adapters implementation.\",\n    \"2026-03-04 Priya Singh (QA): Ran E2E on two historical candidates; conditional outcomes appear in Console UI mock. Need better callouts for perf regression magnitude (absolute vs relative).\",\n    \"2026-03-06 Jonah Park (SRE): Concern: auto-tagging could cause noisy tags if canary telemetry lags. Proposal: require telemetry freshness check before tagging. Marcus will add freshness check to the adapter.\",\n    \"2026-03-08 Lina Chen (PM): Approved prioritization for weekly cadence lane. Requested that LTS promotion remain manual for now and that release notes include runtime upgrade impact section.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Implemented metadata annotation on git tags and wired provenance log. Opening PR for rules engine; feedback requested from SRE and PM on hard gate thresholds.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"tasks\",\n    \"notes\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_6c5c574ffa31475a965aacd0948f00e2\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: stabilization-window-rc-eligibility-orchestrator\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-12876-stabilization-window-rc-eligibility-orchestrator.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: release-train-2026\nTeam: engineering\n\nhigh level proposal : - stabilization window : run a deterministic 48 - hour window after each weekly build where the orchestrator aggregates signals and computes an \" eligibility _ score \" per build. signals include flaky test score ( 30 % ), canary slo delta ( 30 % ), per - token latency regression ( 20 % ), eval - suite regression rate ( 15 % ), and security policy scans ( 5 % ). - rc eligibility rules engine : translate score + hard gates into an outcome : eligible / conditional / blocked. hard gates : critical test failures, policy scan failures, or > 2 % canary slo regression = > blocked. conditional builds require human review. - rc tagging automation : for eligible builds, create a lightweight release branch and annotate with metadata ( build id, score",

{
  "key": "ENG-12876",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "stabilization-window-rc-eligibility-orchestrator",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-01",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-10",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marco Ruiz",
  "project": "release-train-2026",
  "cycle": "2026-W09",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-15",
  "labels": [
    "release-engineering",
    "rc-automation",
    "lts",
    "observability"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-31247",
    "ENG-52391"
  ],
  "release": "runtime-1.22",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Problem: Our current weekly build -> RC tagging flow relies on ad-hoc human checks and a separate release notes generation step. This causes two recurring issues: 1) borderline builds get promoted without a predictable stability gate, increasing hotfix churn on LTS lanes; 2) release notes are assembled manually from PR templates and often miss runtime-impacting changes (batching, KV cache, kernel selection) unless authors explicitly tag them.\n\nGoal: Implement a stabilization-window + RC eligibility orchestrator that programmatically evaluates candidate weekly builds across signal tiers (test flakes, canary SLO deltas, perf regressions, eval quality checks) and produces: (a) an explicit RC candidate list with provenance and confidence score; (b) automated RC tagging in git for eligible candidates; (c) automated release notes draft enriched with runtime-impact metadata and links to performance dashboards. The orchestrator should also expose a small human review UI in Console to approve/override candidates before final tagging for the weekly LTS lane.\n\nHigh level proposal:\n- Stabilization window: run a deterministic 48-hour window after each weekly build where the orchestrator aggregates signals and computes an \"eligibility_score\" per build. Signals include flaky test score (30%), canary SLO delta (30%), per-token latency regression (20%), eval-suite regression rate (15%), and security policy scans (5%).\n- RC eligibility rules engine: translate score + hard gates into an outcome: eligible/conditional/blocked. Hard gates: critical test failures, policy scan failures, or >2% canary SLO regression => blocked. Conditional builds require human review.\n- RC tagging automation: for eligible builds, create a lightweight release branch and annotate with metadata (build id, score, signal links), then tag git as rc-{semver}-{date}. If conditional, mark in Console and create a reviewer assignment.\n- Release notes automation: use PR metadata, label heuristics, and runtime changelog parsers (scan commit messages for keys like BATCHING, KV_CACHE, KERNEL) to synthesize a structured notes draft. Enrich with links to: perf dashboard (grafana), integration test run (CI URL), and eval diff (s3 path). Also include a human-editable summary in Console.\n\nNon-goals: full replacement of human judgment for exceptional releases; automatic LTS promotion without explicit approval.\n\nTrade-offs considered:\n- Strict numeric gating vs. fuzzy scoring: chosen hybrid (score + hard gates) to balance automation with engineer oversight.\n- Time window length: 48h is a compromise between fast weekly cadence and collecting meaningful stability signals. Can be tuned via config.\n- Complexity of release-note NLP: initial implementation will be rule-based heuristics to keep scope small; later iterations may add ML-based grouping.\n\nOperational notes:\n- The orchestrator will run as a daily job in the release namespace and listen for new weekly build events.\n- All decisions are recorded in a release provenance log with links to artifacts for audit.\n- Console feature flags will gate auto-tagging and the human-review UI so we can do staged rollout to internal teams first.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Orchestrator aggregates signals and computes eligibility score for a weekly build within 1 hour of window close",
    "Eligible builds are auto-tagged with RC tags in main git repository when auto-tagging feature flag is enabled",
    "Conditional builds surface in Console with reviewer assignment and a concise provenance panel",
    "Release notes draft is generated for every candidate and includes links to perf dashboard, CI run, and eval diff",
    "All decisions are logged and queryable via the release provenance dashboard"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    "Design eligibility scoring formula and threshold defaults (owner: Marco)",
    "Implement signal adapters: flaky test score (CI), canary SLO delta (telemetry), perf regression extractor (perf infra)",
    "Build rules engine and mapping to eligible/conditional/blocked outcomes",
    "Implement git tagging flow + metadata annotation service",
    "Create release-notes synthesizer with PR label and commit tag heuristics",
    "Console: small review UI and feature flag for auto-tagging",
    "Add audit log entries to provenance store and wire to existing release dashboard",
    "End-to-end QA run on internal staging with three weekly builds"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Per discussion with PM (Lina Chen) we must include explicit canary SLO delta links so on-call can trace regressions quickly",
    "Initial score weights were tuned after running the formula over the last 12 weeks of historical builds; see spreadsheet in Confluence",
    "We plan to gate auto-tagging behind 'release.auto_tag' feature flag and enable only for non-LTS lanes initially",
    "Ops request: include an 'escape hatch' playbook that allows immediate manual un-tag + emergency hotfix flow",
    "Security scanning adapter will surface policy failures but not block RC tagging until we complete remediation workflow (follow-up ticket)"
  ],
  "links": [
    "Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELEASE/pages/RC+Eligibility+Orchestrator",
    "Design doc draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/rc-eligibility-design",
    "Perf dashboard (example): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/perf/weekly-builds?orgId=1",
    "CI flaky score job: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/flaky-score",
    "GitHub PR for prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/412",
    "Release provenance dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/releases/provenance"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-02 Marco Ruiz: Initial spike completed. Scored last 12 weekly builds locally \u2014 score correlates with post-release hotfix count (r=0.68). Moving to adapters implementation.",
    "2026-03-04 Priya Singh (QA): Ran E2E on two historical candidates; conditional outcomes appear in Console UI mock. Need better callouts for perf regression magnitude (absolute vs relative).",
    "2026-03-06 Jonah Park (SRE): Concern: auto-tagging could cause noisy tags if canary telemetry lags. Proposal: require telemetry freshness check before tagging. Marcus will add freshness check to the adapter.",
    "2026-03-08 Lina Chen (PM): Approved prioritization for weekly cadence lane. Requested that LTS promotion remain manual for now and that release notes include runtime upgrade impact section.",
    "2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Implemented metadata annotation on git tags and wired provenance log. Opening PR for rules engine; feedback requested from SRE and PM on hard gate thresholds."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "tasks",
    "notes",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_6c5c574ffa31475a965aacd0948f00e2"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"meeting_id\": \"ff-20250211-001\",\n  \"recorded_at\": \"2025-02-11T16:00:00-08:00\",\n  \"duration_minutes\": \"40\",\n  \"call_type\": \"other\",\n  \"title\": \"Candidate Interview: Senior Sales Engineer\",\n  \"redwood_owner\": \"Sophie Martinez\",\n  \"redwood_attendees\": [\n    \"Sophie Martinez\",\n    \"Evan Liu\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_company\": \"Candidate: Priya Rao\",\n  \"customer_attendees\": [\n    \"Priya Rao (Candidate)\",\n    \"Leah Kim (Recruiter)\"\n  ],\n  \"transcription_quality\": \"medium\",\n  \"summary\": \"First-stage technical interview for a Senior Sales Engineer candidate. Covered candidate background, systems experience, brief product walkthrough, and a short troubleshooting scenario. Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.\",\n  \"topics\": [\n    \"background and experience\",\n    \"technical troubleshooting scenario\",\n    \"Redwood product fit\",\n    \"next steps and scheduling\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18\",\n    \"Recruiter to confirm candidate availability\"\n  ],\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14\",\n    \"Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13\"\n  ],\n  \"competitors_mentioned\": [\n    \"Databricks\",\n    \"Anthropic\"\n  ],\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting Header:\\nDate: 2025-02-11\\nTime: 16:00 PST\\nDuration: 40 minutes\\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\\n\\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\\u2014consistent with KMS policies\\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\\n\\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \\\"K-V cash\\\").\",\n  \"dataset_noise_document\": true,\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"transcript\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2c9dcc3afa3249f39c725884e5be5c72\"\n}",
