{
  "meeting_id": "ff-20250211-001",
  "recorded_at": "2025-02-11T16:00:00-08:00",
  "duration_minutes": "40",
  "call_type": "other",
  "title": "Candidate Interview: Senior Sales Engineer",
  "redwood_owner": "Sophie Martinez",
  "redwood_attendees": [
    "Sophie Martinez",
    "Evan Liu"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Candidate: Priya Rao",
  "customer_attendees": [
    "Priya Rao (Candidate)",
    "Leah Kim (Recruiter)"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",
  "summary": "First-stage technical interview for a Senior Sales Engineer candidate. Covered candidate background, systems experience, brief product walkthrough, and a short troubleshooting scenario. Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.",
  "topics": [
    "background and experience",
    "technical troubleshooting scenario",
    "Redwood product fit",
    "next steps and scheduling"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12",
    "Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18",
    "Recruiter to confirm candidate availability"
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12",
    "Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14",
    "Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13"
  ],
  "competitors_mentioned": [
    "Databricks",
    "Anthropic"
  ],
  "transcript": "Meeting Header:\nDate: 2025-02-11\nTime: 16:00 PST\nDuration: 40 minutes\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\n\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\u2014consistent with KMS policies\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\n\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \"K-V cash\").",

  "content_field_names": [
    "summary",
    "transcript"
  ],

    "content": "{\n  \"meeting_id\": \"ff-20260910-nexora-01\",\n  \"recorded_at\": \"2026-09-10T15:30:00Z\",\n  \"duration_minutes\": \"48\",\n  \"call_type\": \"poc_checkin\",\n  \"title\": \"Nexora Pilot Week 4 - Security Handoff & Retention Review\",\n  \"redwood_owner\": \"Samir Patel\",\n  \"redwood_attendees\": [\n    \"Samir Patel (AE)\",\n    \"Jules Moreno (SE)\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_company\": \"Nexora AI\",\n  \"customer_attendees\": [\n    \"Lena Ortiz (Head of AI Ops)\",\n    \"Markus Rhee (Security Architect)\",\n    \"Priya Desai (Engineering Manager)\"\n  ],\n  \"transcription_quality\": \"medium\",\n  \"competitors_mentioned\": [\n    \"Anthropic\",\n    \"AstraInfer\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Samir to send SOC 2 Type II evidence pack and retention matrix\",\n    \"Jules to run KV cache / burst benchmark and share raw results\",\n    \"Markus to provide SAML IdP metadata and preferred test window\",\n    \"Priya to confirm PII filtering rules and minimum retention period\"\n  ],\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Samir Patel: Send SOC2 pack + retention matrix - due 2026-09-15\",\n    \"Jules Moreno: Run KV cache + burst benchmark, upload results - due 2026-09-17\",\n    \"Markus Rhee (Nexora): Provide SAML metadata and test account window - due 2026-09-14\",\n    \"Priya Desai (Nexora): Finalize list of sensitive fields and retention SLAs - due 2026-09-16\"\n  ],\n  \"crm_deal_id\": \"NX-2026-09-poc-0043\",\n  \"topics\": [\n    \"SSO / SAML setup\",\n    \"Audit logs and retention\",\n    \"SOC 2 evidence & controls\",\n    \"Data residency and PII filtering\",\n    \"Performance tuning (KV cache, batching)\"\n  ],\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting header:\\n- Date/Time: 2026-09-10 15:30 UTC\\n- Duration: ~48 minutes\\n- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Lena (Nexora), Markus (Nexora Sec), Priya (Nexora Eng)\\n\\nSummary: quick handoff from SE to security owner; reviewed SSO steps, audit log exposure and retention windows; agreed on SOC2 docs to share; scheduled benchmarks and test windows. A few items flagged for follow-up: SAML metadata, retention matrix, KV cache benchmark.\\n\\nTranscript:\\n[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Friday. quick agenda \\u2014 security handoff, we wanna cover SSO SAML, audit logs retention, and any SOC Two evidence requests. anyone on from Nexora wants to add?\\n[00:12] Lena (Nexora): yeah thanks, uh, quick one, we wanted to make sure the pilot telemetry that you expose is sufficient for compliance, and then second we wanna lock in the retention windows for PII.\\n[00:22] Jules (Redwood): great, i can walk through the audit log surface \\u2014 there are event streams for request headers, model selection, token counts, and redact flags. logs are available through the console or delivered to your S3-like bucket, and we can route them to your SIEM.\\n[00:36] Markus (Nexora): when you say redact flags, is that server-side PII redaction or client-side markers? we need that clarified for audit.\\n[00:44] Jules (Redwood): good call \\u2014 currently we provide markers (meta) and we also have an optional server-side PII scrubber that we can enable in pilot. it's rule-based today, config lives in the private deployment layer, but for hosted pilots we can enable a pre-send filter. it's not perfect, sometimes names slip, so we advise a combination of client-side tokenization + our filter.\\n[01:10] Priya (Nexora): ok and do those logs include full prompts? we can't keep raw prompts beyond our retention window.\\n[01:18] Jules (Redwood): logs capture prompt hash and truncated context by default. full-prompt capture is opt-in and we can deliver it encrypted with K M S integration, or avoid storing it entirely. for the pilot we recommended storing only hashes + truncated context to meet minimal audit needs.\\n[01:36] Samir (Redwood): Markus, from a security architect perspective what's the hill you need us to clear to be comfortable?\\n[01:44] Markus (Nexora): two things \\u2014 1) SAML SSO: we need IdP metadata exchange and a test window to validate assertion attributes (nameid, email, group). 2) audit logs: we need tamper-evident logs and a retention guarantee for 24 months, with export to our S3 with server-side encryption. also we need evidence that keys are rotated and K M S is used.\\n[02:12] Samir (Redwood): got it. we do support SAML and can provide S P metadata; we also have audit log delivery with SSE and we support key rotation \\u2014 i'll send the SOC2 pack for details on controls.\\n[02:28] Lena (Nexora): what's in that SOC Two pack? is it recent?\\n[02:33] Samir (Redwood): it's SOC 2 Type II, covers the last 12 months; includes control narrative, auditor report, and list of policies. i'll bundle it with a retention matrix that outlines where logs live and encryption at rest / transit.\\n[02:46] Priya (Nexora): sweet. on the performance side i want to align the bench \\u2014 Jules you were going to run KV cache / burst tests to ensure latency doesn't spike when we hit 40 requests per second.\\n[02:56] Jules (Redwood): yes \\u2014 on our side we'll run a workload that mirrors your 1.5k daily active agent sessions, with bursts to 60 RPS. we'll capture p50/p90/p99, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization. note: sometimes the K V cache warm-up can cause initial tail latency \\u2014 we can tune the prefix caching TTL and batching to mitigate.\\n[03:20] Lena (Nexora): any gotchas around private vs hosted? we prefer hosted for speed but security may push us to dedicated or private.\\n[03:28] Samir (Redwood): that's the tradeoff \\u2014 hosted gets you fastest onboarding and telemetry hooks, dedicated gives you VLAN/VPC isolation and customer-managed K M S. during pilot we can run hosted with strict retention & IdP integration, then move to dedicated for final.\\n[03:44] Markus (Nexora): we need a plan B if hosted can't meet our keys requirement. what's minimum time to switch to dedicated?\\n[03:52] Jules (Redwood): in our experience, config and capacity pre-provisioning takes 2-3 weeks once contract and sizing are nailed. we can also provide temporary VPN for audits during pilot to review logs in-place.\\n[04:06] [00:04:06] Samir (Redwood): quick note \\u2014 we sometimes see transcription in these calls mix up VPC as V P C or K V cache as \\\"kiv cache\\\" \\u2014 just ignore the transcript, details in the docs.\\n[04:16] Markus (Nexora): ha, yeah those auto-transcripts are always fun.\\n\\n[05:00] Jules (Redwood): tagging some specifics \\u2014 SAML attributes: we expect nameid, mail, groups. we map groups to RBAC roles in the console; we support SCIM for provisioning but not enabled in pilot by default.\\n[05:14] Priya (Nexora): we do want SCIM later \\u2014 do you have an estimated ETA?\\n[05:19] Jules (Redwood): SCIM is available on Dedicated; for hosted pilots we can do manual provisioning, or enable SCIM in beta if necessary \\u2014 need a short scoping call.\\n\\n[08:10] Lena (Nexora): audit log schema \\u2014 can you show an example?\\n[08:17] Jules (Redwood): sure \\u2014 example event: timestamp, request_id, model_id, token_count, prompt_hash, redaction_flag, user_id (anon if requested), and route. payloads are JSON lines. we can watermarked tamper-evidence by signing log batches.\\n[08:40] Markus (Nexora): the signing \\u2014 is the signature proof verifiable? we need to attest integrity if we hand over log batches to auditors.\\n[08:48] Jules (Redwood): yes, we can provide signed bundles with a checksum and public key verification. we'll include instructions in the SOC docs.\\n\\n[12:05] Samir (Redwood): okay, let's talk retention policy \\u2014 Nexora mentioned 24 months for audit logs, but 90 days for full prompts and 365 for derived embeddings? what's your current desired split?\\n[12:18] Priya (Nexora): suggested baseline: full prompts 90 days, logs 24 months, embeddings 1 year, extracted PII fields removed immediately after extraction unless flagged.\\n[12:29] Markus (Nexora): also need the ability to run on-demand deletion requests (subject access) and an API for that.\\n[12:36] Jules (Redwood): we support selective deletions via an API, and in private deployments we can run a deletion job against the persistent stores. hosted pilot also supports on-demand deletion but we may need a ticket depending on retention tier.\\n\\n[16:00] Lena (Nexora): one small compliance question \\u2014 does your audit trail include admin actions in the console (rollouts, model switches)?\\n[16:08] Jules (Redwood): yes, admin activity is logged. we keep a separate admin audit trail which is also exportable and retains actor metadata.\\n\\n[20:00] Priya (Nexora): for the benchmark \\u2014 what inputs do you need from us?\\n[20:06] Jules (Redwood): ideally: representative prompt sets (anonymized), expected RPS profile, desired max latency SLOs, and a list of model variants to exercise. we'll provision a test harness and replay traffic.\\n[20:18] Priya (Nexora): ok we'll upload a sanitized prompt set to the shared drive.\\n\\n[24:00] Samir (Redwood): ops/pricing \\u2014 Markus asked about the cost delta between hosted with retention guarantees vs dedicated. ballpark numbers?\\n[24:12] Samir (Redwood): hosted with extended retention and K M S on our side is roughly +15% on unit cost, dedicated (customer-managed keys and VPC) is larger \\u2014 depends on reserved capacity commitments. we'll follow up with a tailored pricing sheet.\\n[24:28] Markus (Nexora): that's fine, as long as it's predictable for budgeting.\\n\\n[30:00] Jules (Redwood): technical note \\u2014 the KV cache warm-up is important: recommend TTL prewarm for sessions where you expect sustained interactions. also batching parameters: aggressive batching saves cost but increases p50; we can tune per-route.\\n[30:18] Priya (Nexora): can you provide default batching/ttl settings?\\n[30:22] Jules (Redwood): yes i'll share our recommended config (example: batch_window_ms:20, max_batch_tokens:4096, kv_cache_ttl:600s) \\u2014 just examples; we'll run bench to tune.\\n\\n[36:00] Samir (Redwood): security docs deliverable timeline \\u2014 i'll send SOC2 + control narratives by next Wednesday. Jules will push the benchmark spreadsheet by Friday. Markus, can you confirm IdP metadata by Monday?\\n[36:16] Markus (Nexora): Monday works, we need a four hour window Tuesday afternoon for assertion testing.\\n[36:24] Samir (Redwood): noted, we will schedule that test window.\\n\\n[40:00] Lena (Nexora): any blocker on the ability to export logs to our S3 with SSE?\\n[40:06] Jules (Redwood): none, we support S3 export with SSE-C or SSE-S3 and cross-account role. we'll document the required IAM policy.\\n\\n[44:00] Samir (Redwood): quick recap / next steps \\u2014 action items listed in the doc. we'll reconvene on Monday only if needed after the SAML handoff; otherwise next sync is our end-of-week bench review.\\n[44:18] Priya (Nexora): sounds good. thanks everyone.\\n[44:24] Markus (Nexora): thanks.\\n[44:30] Jules (Redwood): thanks all, we'll follow up with the files.\\n\\nEnd of transcript.\\n\\nNotes / Links mentioned: \\n- SOC2 pack (to be sent)\\n- SAML metadata exchange link (to be shared)\\n- Benchmark spreadsheet (to be uploaded by Jules)\\n- Shared drive: https://drive.internal/nexora-pilot (placeholder)\\n\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"transcript\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_eb6e9aeb654646528cb7553a4dbef0e9\"\n}",

{

  "title": "Nexora Pilot Week 4 - Security Handoff & Retention Review",
  "redwood_owner": "Samir Patel",

    "Jules Moreno (SE)"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Nexora AI",

    "Lena Ortiz (Head of AI Ops)",
    "Markus Rhee (Security Architect)",
    "Priya Desai (Engineering Manager)"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",

    "Anthropic",
    "AstraInfer"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Samir to send SOC 2 Type II evidence pack and retention matrix",
    "Jules to run KV cache / burst benchmark and share raw results",
    "Markus to provide SAML IdP metadata and preferred test window",
    "Priya to confirm PII filtering rules and minimum retention period"
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Samir Patel: Send SOC2 pack + retention matrix - due 2026-09-15",
    "Jules Moreno: Run KV cache + burst benchmark, upload results - due 2026-09-17",
    "Markus Rhee (Nexora): Provide SAML metadata and test account window - due 2026-09-14",
    "Priya Desai (Nexora): Finalize list of sensitive fields and retention SLAs - due 2026-09-16"
  ],
  "crm_deal_id": "NX-2026-09-poc-0043",
  "topics": [
    "SSO / SAML setup",
    "Audit logs and retention",
    "SOC 2 evidence & controls",
    "Data residency and PII filtering",
    "Performance tuning (KV cache, batching)"
  ],
  "transcript": "Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-10 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Lena (Nexora), Markus (Nexora Sec), Priya (Nexora Eng)

Summary: quick handoff from SE to security owner; reviewed SSO steps, audit log exposure and retention windows; agreed on SOC2 docs to share; scheduled benchmarks and test windows. A few items flagged for follow-up: SAML metadata, retention matrix, KV cache benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Friday. quick agenda — security handoff, we wanna cover SSO SAML, audit logs retention, and any SOC Two evidence requests. anyone on from Nexora wants to add?
[00:12] Lena (Nexora): yeah thanks, uh, quick one, we wanted to make sure the pilot telemetry that you expose is sufficient for compliance, and then second we wanna lock in the retention windows for PII.
[00:22] Jules (Redwood): great, i can walk through the audit log surface — there are event streams for request headers, model selection, token counts, and redact flags. logs are available through the console or delivered to your S3-like bucket, and we can route them to your SIEM.
[00:36] Markus (Nexora): when you say redact flags, is that server-side PII redaction or client-side markers? we need that clarified for audit.
[00:44] Jules (Redwood): good call — currently we provide markers (meta) and we also have an optional server-side PII scrubber that we can enable in pilot. it's rule-based today, config lives in the private deployment layer, but for hosted pilots we can enable a pre-send filter. it's not perfect, sometimes names slip, so we advise a combination of client-side tokenization + our filter.
[01:10] Priya (Nexora): ok and do those logs include full prompts? we can't keep raw prompts beyond our retention window.
[01:18] Jules (Redwood): logs capture prompt hash and truncated context by default. full-prompt capture is opt-in and we can deliver it encrypted with K M S integration, or avoid storing it entirely. for the pilot we recommended storing only hashes + truncated context to meet minimal audit needs.
[01:36] Samir (Redwood): Markus, from a security architect perspective what's the hill you need us to clear to be comfortable?
[01:44] Markus (Nexora): two things — 1) SAML SSO: we need IdP metadata exchange and a test window to validate assertion attributes (nameid, email, group). 2) audit logs: we need tamper-evident logs and a retention guarantee for 24 months, with export to our S3 with server-side encryption. also we need evidence that keys are rotated and K M S is used.
[02:12] Samir (Redwood): got it. we do support SAML and can provide S P metadata; we also have audit log delivery with SSE and we support key rotation — i'll send the SOC2 pack for details on controls.
[02:28] Lena (Nexora): what's in that SOC Two pack? is it recent?
[02:33] Samir (Redwood): it's SOC 2 Type II, covers the last 12 months; includes control narrative, auditor report, and list of policies. i'll bundle it with a retention matrix that outlines where logs live and encryption at rest / transit.
[02:46] Priya (Nexora): sweet. on the performance side i want to align the bench — Jules you were going to run KV cache / burst tests to ensure latency doesn't spike when we hit 40 requests per second.
[02:56] Jules (Redwood): yes — on our side we'll run a workload that mirrors your 1.5k daily active agent sessions, with bursts to 60 RPS. we'll capture p50/p90/p99, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization. note: sometimes the K V cache warm-up can cause initial tail latency — we can tune the prefix caching TTL and batching to mitigate.
[03:20] Lena (Nexora): any gotchas around private vs hosted? we prefer hosted for speed but security may push us to dedicated or private.
[03:28] Samir (Redwood): that's the tradeoff — hosted gets you fastest onboarding and telemetry hooks, dedicated gives you VLAN/VPC isolation and customer-managed K M S. during pilot we can run hosted with strict retention & IdP integration, then move to dedicated for final.
[03:44] Markus (Nexora): we need a plan B if hosted can't meet our keys requirement. what's minimum time to switch to dedicated?
[03:52] Jules (Redwood): in our experience, config and capacity pre-provisioning takes 2-3 weeks once contract and sizing are nailed. we can also provide temporary VPN for audits during pilot to review logs in-place.
[04:06] [00:04:06] Samir (Redwood): quick note — we sometimes see transcription in these calls mix up VPC as V P C or K V cache as "kiv cache" — just ignore the transcript, details in the docs.
[04:16] Markus (Nexora): ha, yeah those auto-transcripts are always fun.

[05:00] Jules (Redwood): tagging some specifics — SAML attributes: we expect nameid, mail, groups. we map groups to RBAC roles in the console; we support SCIM for provisioning but not enabled in pilot by default.
[05:14] Priya (Nexora): we do want SCIM later — do you have an estimated ETA?
[05:19] Jules (Redwood): SCIM is available on Dedicated; for hosted pilots we can do manual provisioning, or enable SCIM in beta if necessary — need a short scoping call.

[08:10] Lena (Nexora): audit log schema — can you show an example?
[08:17] Jules (Redwood): sure — example event: timestamp, request_id, model_id, token_count, prompt_hash, redaction_flag, user_id (anon if requested), and route. payloads are JSON lines. we can watermarked tamper-evidence by signing log batches.
[08:40] Markus (Nexora): the signing — is the signature proof verifiable? we need to attest integrity if we hand over log batches to auditors.
[08:48] Jules (Redwood): yes, we can provide signed bundles with a checksum and public key verification. we'll include instructions in the SOC docs.

[12:05] Samir (Redwood): okay, let's talk retention policy — Nexora mentioned 24 months for audit logs, but 90 days for full prompts and 365 for derived embeddings? what's your current desired split?
[12:18] Priya (Nexora): suggested baseline: full prompts 90 days, logs 24 months, embeddings 1 year, extracted PII fields removed immediately after extraction unless flagged.
[12:29] Markus (Nexora): also need the ability to run on-demand deletion requests (subject access) and an API for that.
[12:36] Jules (Redwood): we support selective deletions via an API, and in private deployments we can run a deletion job against the persistent stores. hosted pilot also supports on-demand deletion but we may need a ticket depending on retention tier.

[16:00] Lena (Nexora): one small compliance question — does your audit trail include admin actions in the console (rollouts, model switches)?
[16:08] Jules (Redwood): yes, admin activity is logged. we keep a separate admin audit trail which is also exportable and retains actor metadata.

[20:00] Priya (Nexora): for the benchmark — what inputs do you need from us?
[20:06] Jules (Redwood): ideally: representative prompt sets (anonymized), expected RPS profile, desired max latency SLOs, and a list of model variants to exercise. we'll provision a test harness and replay traffic.
[20:18] Priya (Nexora): ok we'll upload a sanitized prompt set to the shared drive.

[24:00] Samir (Redwood): ops/pricing — Markus asked about the cost delta between hosted with retention guarantees vs dedicated. ballpark numbers?
[24:12] Samir (Redwood): hosted with extended retention and K M S on our side is roughly +15% on unit cost, dedicated (customer-managed keys and VPC) is larger — depends on reserved capacity commitments. we'll follow up with a tailored pricing sheet.
[24:28] Markus (Nexora): that's fine, as long as it's predictable for budgeting.

[30:00] Jules (Redwood): technical note — the KV cache warm-up is important: recommend TTL prewarm for sessions where you expect sustained interactions. also batching parameters: aggressive batching saves cost but increases p50; we can tune per-route.
[30:18] Priya (Nexora): can you provide default batching/ttl settings?
[30:22] Jules (Redwood): yes i'll share our recommended config (example: batch_window_ms:20, max_batch_tokens:4096, kv_cache_ttl:600s) — just examples; we'll run bench to tune.

[36:00] Samir (Redwood): security docs deliverable timeline — i'll send SOC2 + control narratives by next Wednesday. Jules will push the benchmark spreadsheet by Friday. Markus, can you confirm IdP metadata by Monday?
[36:16] Markus (Nexora): Monday works, we need a four hour window Tuesday afternoon for assertion testing.
[36:24] Samir (Redwood): noted, we will schedule that test window.

[40:00] Lena (Nexora): any blocker on the ability to export logs to our S3 with SSE?
[40:06] Jules (Redwood): none, we support S3 export with SSE-C or SSE-S3 and cross-account role. we'll document the required IAM policy.

[44:00] Samir (Redwood): quick recap / next steps — action items listed in the doc. we'll reconvene on Monday only if needed after the SAML handoff; otherwise next sync is our end-of-week bench review.
[44:18] Priya (Nexora): sounds good. thanks everyone.
[44:24] Markus (Nexora): thanks.
[44:30] Jules (Redwood): thanks all, we'll follow up with the files.

End of transcript.

Notes / Links mentioned: 
- SOC2 pack (to be sent)
- SAML metadata exchange link (to be shared)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (to be uploaded by Jules)
- Shared drive: https://drive.internal/nexora-pilot (placeholder)

high level proposal : - stabilization window : run a deterministic 48 - hour window after each weekly build where the orchestrator aggregates signals and computes an " eligibility _ score " per build. signals include flaky test score ( 30 % ), canary slo delta ( 30 % ), per - token latency regression ( 20 % ), eval - suite regression rate ( 15 % ), and security policy scans ( 5 % ). - rc eligibility rules engine : translate score + hard gates into an outcome : eligible / conditional / blocked. hard gates : critical test failures, policy scan failures, or > 2 % canary slo regression = > blocked. conditional builds require human review. - rc tagging automation : for eligible builds, create a lightweight release branch and annotate with metadata ( build id, score

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-ml\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1760004322\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1760004322\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1760004442\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"jia\",\n    \"mike\",\n    \"sara\",\n    \"oliver\",\n    \"bench-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"jia: Quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline tradeoffs \\u2014 thinking about moving the heavy bench (full golden/regression eval) to async post-accept, and keep the fast adapter/tokenizer checks sync at intake. Thoughts?\\n\\nmike: Agree in principle. Main risk is we accept models that pass lightweight checks but fail the heavy bench later => downstream quality incidents. We need mitigations: canary traffic + auto-rollback and a clear quarantine state.\\n\\nsara: Proposal: two-phase acceptance. 1) intake sync smoke: tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass, tiny perf check. 2) gated async bench: full golden + regression eval on reserved bench pool. If async fails, mark model as `quarantine` and block routing. Also need a narrow interface between intake and bench for signals.\\n\\noliver: Important note \\u2014 keep a compact \\\"fast-probe\\\" golden set in intake (~50 inputs) to catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer encodings, padding, EOS behavior). That will reduce wasteful async runs. Bench infra should emit categorical verdicts: accept / flag / critical-fail.\\n\\njia: How should we version golden artifacts? If intake and async bench use different golden sets we risk false positives/negatives. Idea: store `golden_set_id` in model metadata and surface it to runtime & bench.\\n\\nmike: +1. Also: make smoke thresholds intentionally loose; async bench enforces strict thresholds. For rollout, use shadow traffic + small canaries to validate behavior on real queries before full promotion.\\n\\nsara: API contract sketch: intake returns a candidate_id. Bench polls /bench-status?candidate_id or we push a webhook. Bench status payload should include: status, failed_tests[], drift_score, latency_p95, golden_set_id. Example minimal payload:\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"candidate_id\\\": \\\"cand-2026-03-01-42\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"quarantine\\\",\\n  \\\"failed_tests\\\": [\\\"regression:qa-v2\\\"],\\n  \\\"drift_score\\\": \\\"0.32\\\",\\n  \\\"latency_p95_ms\\\": \\\"312\\\",\\n  \\\"golden_set_id\\\": \\\"gold-2026-02-15-v3\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nbench-bot: Bench job queued: candidate_id=cand-2026-03-01-42, estimated_gpu_hours=3, expected_completion=~6h. Status webhook will fire to intake when done.\\n\\noliver: Ops checklist: we need cost caps for async bench (max GPU-hours per org/day) and a fallback if bench never completes (e.g., pending >24h => auto-reject or require human override). Also consider prioritization queue for high-risk customers.\\n\\njia: Noted. I'll draft a short RFC with proposed API surface, lifecycle states (candidate -> accepted_pending_bench -> accepted / quarantine / rejected), and rollout recipe (shadow -> small canary -> ramp). Will include golden_set versioning + sample inputs for intake. Volunteers to review the RFC? :coffee:\\nmike: I'll review. :+1:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f853f992f7a0416ea9ab1c2b287f61dc\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "channel": "eng-ml",
  "thread_ts": "1760004322",
  "first_message_ts": "1760004322",
  "last_message_ts": "1760004442",
  "participants": [
    "jia",
    "mike",
    "sara",
    "oliver",
    "bench-bot"
  ],
  "text": "jia: Quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline tradeoffs — thinking about moving the heavy bench (full golden/regression eval) to async post-accept, and keep the fast adapter/tokenizer checks sync at intake. Thoughts?

mike: Agree in principle. Main risk is we accept models that pass lightweight checks but fail the heavy bench later => downstream quality incidents. We need mitigations: canary traffic + auto-rollback and a clear quarantine state.

sara: Proposal: two-phase acceptance. 1) intake sync smoke: tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass, tiny perf check. 2) gated async bench: full golden + regression eval on reserved bench pool. If async fails, mark model as `quarantine` and block routing. Also need a narrow interface between intake and bench for signals.

oliver: Important note — keep a compact "fast-probe" golden set in intake (~50 inputs) to catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer encodings, padding, EOS behavior). That will reduce wasteful async runs. Bench infra should emit categorical verdicts: accept / flag / critical-fail.

jia: How should we version golden artifacts? If intake and async bench use different golden sets we risk false positives/negatives. Idea: store `golden_set_id` in model metadata and surface it to runtime & bench.

mike: +1. Also: make smoke thresholds intentionally loose; async bench enforces strict thresholds. For rollout, use shadow traffic + small canaries to validate behavior on real queries before full promotion.

sara: API contract sketch: intake returns a candidate_id. Bench polls /bench-status?candidate_id or we push a webhook. Bench status payload should include: status, failed_tests[], drift_score, latency_p95, golden_set_id. Example minimal payload:
```json
{
  "candidate_id": "cand-2026-03-01-42",
  "status": "quarantine",
  "failed_tests": ["regression:qa-v2"],
  "drift_score": "0.32",
  "latency_p95_ms": "312",
  "golden_set_id": "gold-2026-02-15-v3"
}
```

bench-bot: Bench job queued: candidate_id=cand-2026-03-01-42, estimated_gpu_hours=3, expected_completion=~6h. Status webhook will fire to intake when done.

oliver: Ops checklist: we need cost caps for async bench (max GPU-hours per org/day) and a fallback if bench never completes (e.g., pending >24h => auto-reject or require human override). Also consider prioritization queue for high-risk customers.

jia: Noted. I'll draft a short RFC with proposed API surface, lifecycle states (candidate -> accepted_pending_bench -> accepted / quarantine / rejected), and rollout recipe (shadow -> small canary -> ramp). Will include golden_set versioning + sample inputs for intake. Volunteers to review the RFC? :coffee:
mike: I'll review. :+1:",

side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window\",\n    \"Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals\",\n    \"User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)\",\n    \"Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation\",\n    \"Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model\",\n    \"All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV\",\n    \"Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta\"\n  ],\n  \"tasks\": [\n    \"Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)\",\n    \"Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap\",\n    \"Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison\",\n    \"Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests\",\n    \"Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-24680-cohort-comparator-and-trace-linker-for-deployment-health.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: product-management\nProject: Console Rollouts\nTeam: product-management\n\n- comparator ui shows side - by - side cohort - level charts for latency ( p50 / p95 ), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window - diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals - user can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request - level metadata ( route, model version, routing policy, input hash ) - trace linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors ( e. g., model variant, batch size, region ) derived from instrumentation - auto - rollback triggers are visible per - rollout and can be toggled ; console records the reason and suggested fallback model - all",

document.title: Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-24680",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "creator": "Aisha Kapoor",
  "assignee": "Marco Lin",
  "project": "Console Rollouts",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-04-01",
  "labels": [
    "rollouts",
    "observability",
    "console",
    "canary",
    "a/b",
    "auto-rollback",
    "tracing"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-14091"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-20345",
    "ENG-20412",
    "DES-317"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2026.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window",
    "Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals",
    "User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)",
    "Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation",
    "Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model",
    "All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV",
    "Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    "Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)",
    "Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap",
    "Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison",
    "Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests",
    "Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins",
    "SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics",
    "QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios",
    "Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook"
  ],
  "design_assets": [
    "https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype",
    "https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf"
  ],
  "telemetry_queries": [
    "PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m]) by (cohort)",
    "PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))",
    "SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)",
    "Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)",
    "GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow",
    "Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes",
    "Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust",
    "Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis"
  ],
  "tradeoffs": [
    "Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas",
    "Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially",
    "Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Nina Rodriguez (Security)",
    "Omar Patel (SRE)",
    "Leah Chen (Design)",
    "Devon Morris (Engineering lead)"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action",
    "Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate",
    "Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket \u2014 goal is to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions by surface-level correlation -> request-level evidence.",
    "2026-03-11 Marco Lin: Spun up spike; backend will reuse existing metrics pipeline but needs a lightweight join index for cohort -> trace linking (ENG-20345)",
    "2026-03-12 Leah Chen: Uploaded first mockups; recommended adding a confidence ribbon to diff charts to indicate statistical significance",
    "2026-03-13 Omar Patel: SRE flagged potential retention cost issue; recommending adaptive sampling and a 14-day lookback default",
    "2026-03-14 Marco Lin: Marked 'in progress' \u2014 backend API contract drafted and PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128"
  ],
  "attachments": [
    "https://confluence.redwood/internal/Console-Rollouts/Cohort-Comparator-PRD",

    "id": "dsid_f5b6b65ec24e4e19b81c4e96d35bf77c",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-134876-stream-adapter-pluggable-token-provider-cross-sdk-bump.json",
    "title": "Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"134876\",\n  \"title\": \"Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Khan\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-28\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/sdk-cross-adapter-token-provider\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Ethan Walsh\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez\",\n    \"Jordan Lee\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"auth\",\n    \"ergonomics\",\n    \"chore\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4026\",\n    \"ENG-4041\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"12\",\n  \"additions\": \"842\",\n  \"deletions\": \"210\",\n  \"description\": \"This PR introduces a language-agnostic stream-adapter registry and a pluggable token-provider abstraction to the SDK surface so that each SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. Motivation: persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across SDKs were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. The change packages three coordinated pieces: 1) a lightweight StreamAdapterRegistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to SDK adapters; 2) a PluggableTokenProvider interface plus a default refresh provider used by hosted and dedicated customers; 3) thin ergonomic wrappers added to each SDK exposing the provider as an opt-in parameter and a compatibility shim for older code paths. Checklist: - [x] Core registry implementation and protocol contract - [x] Default token provider implementation and short-circuit for static tokens - [x] SDK wrappers: python client convenience function, TS builder option, Go functional option - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests for resume/reconnect and single-token refresh paths - [x] Documentation snippets and migration notes - [x] Version bumps for SDK packages (python/ts/go) Compatibility notes: the adapters are opt-in by default; existing call sites continue to work. To enable the new behavior set `stream_adapter: \\\"registry-v1\\\"` and pass `token_provider` in the client constructor. There is an opt-in migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md. Rollout plan: merge to main, cut a patch release for hosted clients who opt-in, coordinate SDK releases in the same week to avoid partial parity. Related work: ENG-4026 (streaming-reconnect stability), ENG-4041 (sdk-auth-resilience).\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"9f2b7a1 - core: add StreamAdapterRegistry and protocol contract\",\n    \"a3d4e02 - auth: introduce PluggableTokenProvider and default refresher\",\n    \"b71c9f3 - sdk/python: expose token_provider param and add thin adapter\",\n    \"c8d20e4 - sdk/typescript: builder option + tests for backpressure semantics\",\n    \"d4f11b5 - sdk/go: functional option + fixes for reconnect double-reauth\",\n    \"e16a332 - tests: cross-sdk integration harness and CI workflow updates\",\n    \"f28b44c - docs: migration guide and example snippets\"\n  ],\n  \"changed_files\": [\n    \"core/streaming/adapter_registry.py\",\n    \"core/auth/token_provider_interface.go\",\n    \"sdk/python/redwood/client.py\",\n    \"sdk/python/tests/test_stream_adapter_integration.py\",\n    \"sdk/typescript/src/stream/builder.ts\",\n    \"sdk/typescript/test/stream/backpressure.spec.ts\",\n    \"sdk/go/options/stream_opt.go\",\n    \"sdk/go/integration/stream_integration_test.go\",\n    \"docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md\",\n    \"ci/workflows/cross-sdk-integration.yml\",\n    \"pkg/versioning/sdk_version_manifest.json\",\n    \"CHANGELOG.md\"\n  ],\n  \"review_thread\": [\n    \"Ethan Walsh: Overall looks good; please add explicit unit tests for the python token refresh race (requester saw double-refresh in prod).\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Added python unit that simulates concurrent KV cache invalidation and verified single refresh path (see new test).\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez: TS builder ergonomics are better but please ensure default builder remains zero-config for existing users.\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Builder defaults preserved; added explicit e2e backpressure test to assert no extra buffering on reconnect.\",\n    \"Jordan Lee: small nit on Go naming and a suggestion to document semantics of the token_provider lifecycle.\",\n    \"Aisha Khan: Renamed method to TokenProviderLifecycle() and added documentation block in sdk/go/README.md.\",\n    \"Marta L\\u00f3pez: CI flaky test (ts/backpressure) failed once; re-ran and it passed. Approving after green CI.\",\n    \"Ethan Walsh: Approved. Verified integration harness reproduced previous double-reauth; new registry fixes scenario.\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit: python - pass\",\n    \"unit: typescript - pass\",\n    \"unit: go - pass\",\n    \"integration: cross-sdk - pass\",\n    \"lint: python/ts/go - pass\",\n    \"e2e: smoke - pass\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merge_commit\": \"squash-merge 7a3d4f (stream-adapter-registry)\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Added a stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers. SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) now accept an optional token_provider for streaming calls to control refresh lifecycle. Opt-in by default. Bugfix: prevents duplicate token refresh during stream reconnects. SDK version bumps: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v0.9.0.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"no\",\n  \"testing\": [\n    \"Local unit tests for each SDK and core (python/ts/go)\",\n    \"Cross-SDK integration harness that drives connect/resume scenarios with deterministic delays\",\n    \"Load-run smoke test to ensure no regression in streaming throughput\",\n    \"Manual verification with a staging Dedicated cluster to validate token rotation under sustained reconnects\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_thread\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f5b6b65ec24e4e19b81c4e96d35bf77c\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-134876-stream-adapter-pluggable-token-provider-cross-sdk-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: redwood\n\ndescription : this pr introduces a language - agnostic stream - adapter registry and a pluggable token - provider abstraction to the sdk surface so that each sdk ( python / typescript / go ) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. motivation : persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across sdks were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. the change packages three coordinated pieces : 1 ) a lightweight streamadapterregistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to sdk adapters ; 2 ) a pluggabletokenprovider interface plus a default refresh provider used",

document.title: Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps
document.content:
{
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "134876",
  "title": "Introduce stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers; cross-SDK ergonomic wrappers and version bumps",
  "author": "Aisha Khan",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-28",
  "merged_at": "2026-03-01",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/sdk-cross-adapter-token-provider",
  "reviewers": [
    "Ethan Walsh",
    "Marta L\u00f3pez",
    "Jordan Lee"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "streaming",
    "auth",
    "ergonomics",
    "chore"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4026",
    "ENG-4041"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "12",
  "additions": "842",
  "deletions": "210",
  "description": "This PR introduces a language-agnostic stream-adapter registry and a pluggable token-provider abstraction to the SDK surface so that each SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) can opt into a shared streaming handshake and reauth strategy without shipping duplicate logic. Motivation: persistent differences in stream handshake timing and token refresh semantics across SDKs were causing duplicate reauth attempts and subtle backpressure mismatches in production. The change packages three coordinated pieces: 1) a lightweight StreamAdapterRegistry in the core redwood library that maps protocol variants to SDK adapters; 2) a PluggableTokenProvider interface plus a default refresh provider used by hosted and dedicated customers; 3) thin ergonomic wrappers added to each SDK exposing the provider as an opt-in parameter and a compatibility shim for older code paths. Checklist: - [x] Core registry implementation and protocol contract - [x] Default token provider implementation and short-circuit for static tokens - [x] SDK wrappers: python client convenience function, TS builder option, Go functional option - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests for resume/reconnect and single-token refresh paths - [x] Documentation snippets and migration notes - [x] Version bumps for SDK packages (python/ts/go) Compatibility notes: the adapters are opt-in by default; existing call sites continue to work. To enable the new behavior set `stream_adapter: \"registry-v1\"` and pass `token_provider` in the client constructor. There is an opt-in migration guide in docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md. Rollout plan: merge to main, cut a patch release for hosted clients who opt-in, coordinate SDK releases in the same week to avoid partial parity. Related work: ENG-4026 (streaming-reconnect stability), ENG-4041 (sdk-auth-resilience).",
  "commits": [
    "9f2b7a1 - core: add StreamAdapterRegistry and protocol contract",
    "a3d4e02 - auth: introduce PluggableTokenProvider and default refresher",
    "b71c9f3 - sdk/python: expose token_provider param and add thin adapter",
    "c8d20e4 - sdk/typescript: builder option + tests for backpressure semantics",
    "d4f11b5 - sdk/go: functional option + fixes for reconnect double-reauth",
    "e16a332 - tests: cross-sdk integration harness and CI workflow updates",
    "f28b44c - docs: migration guide and example snippets"
  ],
  "changed_files": [
    "core/streaming/adapter_registry.py",
    "core/auth/token_provider_interface.go",
    "sdk/python/redwood/client.py",
    "sdk/python/tests/test_stream_adapter_integration.py",
    "sdk/typescript/src/stream/builder.ts",
    "sdk/typescript/test/stream/backpressure.spec.ts",
    "sdk/go/options/stream_opt.go",
    "sdk/go/integration/stream_integration_test.go",
    "docs/sdk-migration/stream-adapter.md",
    "ci/workflows/cross-sdk-integration.yml",
    "pkg/versioning/sdk_version_manifest.json",
    "CHANGELOG.md"
  ],
  "review_thread": [
    "Ethan Walsh: Overall looks good; please add explicit unit tests for the python token refresh race (requester saw double-refresh in prod).",
    "Aisha Khan: Added python unit that simulates concurrent KV cache invalidation and verified single refresh path (see new test).",
    "Marta L\u00f3pez: TS builder ergonomics are better but please ensure default builder remains zero-config for existing users.",
    "Aisha Khan: Builder defaults preserved; added explicit e2e backpressure test to assert no extra buffering on reconnect.",
    "Jordan Lee: small nit on Go naming and a suggestion to document semantics of the token_provider lifecycle.",
    "Aisha Khan: Renamed method to TokenProviderLifecycle() and added documentation block in sdk/go/README.md.",
    "Marta L\u00f3pez: CI flaky test (ts/backpressure) failed once; re-ran and it passed. Approving after green CI.",
    "Ethan Walsh: Approved. Verified integration harness reproduced previous double-reauth; new registry fixes scenario."
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "unit: python - pass",
    "unit: typescript - pass",
    "unit: go - pass",
    "integration: cross-sdk - pass",
    "lint: python/ts/go - pass",
    "e2e: smoke - pass"
  ],
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "merge_commit": "squash-merge 7a3d4f (stream-adapter-registry)",
  "release_notes": "Added a stream-adapter registry and pluggable token providers. SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) now accept an optional token_provider for streaming calls to control refresh lifecycle. Opt-in by default. Bugfix: prevents duplicate token refresh during stream reconnects. SDK version bumps: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v0.9.0.",
  "breaking_change": "no",
  "testing": [
    "Local unit tests for each SDK and core (python/ts/go)",
    "Cross-SDK integration harness that drives connect/resume scenarios with deterministic delays",
    "Load-run smoke test to ensure no regression in streaming throughput",
    "Manual verification with a staging Dedicated cluster to validate token rotation under sustained reconnects"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_thread",
    "release_notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_f5b6b65ec24e4e19b81c4e96d35bf77c"
}

This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.\\n\\nWhy this is exceptional:\\n- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).\\n- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.\\n2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "gmail-soojin-20260818-hc-exc-001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "laura_bennett",
    "markus_klein",
    "neha_kapoor"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Polaris Talent <sarah@polaris-talent.com>",
    "GreenCore migrations (eng@greencore.com)"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "related_links": [
    "JIRA: INFRA-2247",
    "Drive: https://drive.redwood/workspace/platform/migration-risk-matrix"
  ],
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "hc_exception_form.pdf",
    "migration_risk_matrix.xlsx",
    "cost_breakdown_6mo.csv"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Hi Laura / Markus,

Tl;dr: Requesting a one-time hiring-freeze exception to backfill a departing Senior Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) on Platform Services. This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.

Why this is exceptional:
- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).
- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). Migration has hard deadlines tied to customer contract INFRA-2247.
- Impact: with current staffing we estimate +30–45% risk of missing the rollout milestone and elevated on-call burden across two teams.

Proposed path:
1) Approve HC exception to backfill Senior IC (IC4) with either direct hire or 6-month contractor through Polaris Talent (attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv).
2) If approved, prioritize internal candidates first (we have one internal transfer candidate in org).
3) If approval delayed >7 days, we will request temporary time-limited escalation budget for overtime and hiring agency retained search.

Attached: HC exception form (filled), migration risk matrix, six-month cost comparison (direct hire vs contractor).

Ask: Approve or provide guidance on preferred funnel (internal transfer vs external contractor) by EOD Aug 18 so we can start vendor engagement.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Services
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0142

[attachment: hc_exception_form.pdf] [attachment: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx] [attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv]",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13 11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick Qs before I greenlight:

1) Headcount budget: do you have the hiring cost vs committed budget this FY (include recruiting fees if external)? I saw your attachment but would like a one-line delta to the org budget.
2) Coverage plan: if we approve internal transfer, who covers the gaps left by that transfer? (need names/teams).
3) SLA tolerances: quantify the customer impact in $ or churn risk if migration slips by 4 weeks.

If you can get me the answers and sign-off from Finance (Markus) and HR (Neha) by EOD Aug 18 I can approve the exception. If Finance can't commit, consider a 6-month contractor approval as fallback.

— Laura
VP Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 9:15 AM Soojin Lee wrote:...",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-14 08:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Laura — quick follow with the concrete numbers you asked for:

1) Budget delta: direct hire (mid-band IC4) fully loaded = $240k/yr total comp equivalent; recruiting + ramp = ~ $30k in Y1, so net delta to FY budget = +$270k. 6-month contractor via agency = ~$85k (includes agency fee). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.
2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. Proposed mitigation: shift two noncritical tickets to FY27 backlog and assign a 3rd rotation from SRE for 6 weeks.
3) SLA impact: conservative estimate is $120k ARR at risk (single large customer migration) and increased engineering support cost ~$25k in third-party consulting if we miss milestone by 4 weeks.

Attached is an updated one-pager summarizing these points and the requested approval box filled out on the HC exception form. I recommend approving a contractor for 6 months while we run a parallel external search — this minimizes SLA risk and gives time to evaluate internal transfer without blocking the migration schedule.

If you want, I can arrange a short sync with Finance (Markus) and Neha to run through the numbers tomorrow.

— Soojin

[inline: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx excerpt]

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Sarah Miller <sarah@polaris-talent.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14 07:22 -07:00
Subject: Candidate availability

Soojin — we have two senior infra contractors available starting 9/7 and a permanent candidate who could move by late Sept. If you'd like the contractor hold we'll need a 3-day confirmation.

Best,
Sarah
Polaris Talent",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18 16:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

All — reviewed the cost sheet and migration risk matrix. Finance can support a time-limited contractor approval up to $95k for six months on the condition that: 

- Recruiting runs concurrently and we aim for a permanent hire within 4 months,
- Team documents handover & runbooks in the first 30 days (Soojin, please own),
- A post-mortem and budget reconciliation is provided to Finance within 90 days.

Laura — if that's acceptable from your side, consider this the Finance conditional approval. Neha — please confirm any compliance/contracting constraints on short-term contractor engagements and confirm whether Polaris has passed vendor onboarding.

Markus Klein
Director, Finance Planning
Redwood Inference

On Aug 14, 2026, Soojin Lee wrote:..."

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-77120\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Marcus Li\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Elena Rodriguez\",\n  \"project\": \"sdk-function-calls\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-14\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"function-calling\",\n    \"cross-language\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"retry\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-61452\",\n    \"ENG-74290\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"sdk-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators\",\n    \"Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()\",\n    \"Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers\",\n    \"Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion\",\n    \"Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios\",\n    \"Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs\"\n  ],\n  \"design_notes\": [\n    \"Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models\",\n    \"Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation\",\n    \"Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools\",\n    \"Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early\",\n    \"Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure\",\n    \"Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_plan\": [\n    \"Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface\",\n    \"Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)\",\n    \"Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)\",\n    \"Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config\",\n    \"Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support\"\n  ],\n  \"test_plan\": [\n    \"Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays\",\n    \"Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior\",\n    \"Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested\",\n    \"Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead\",\n    \"Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Alpha: release TypeScript reference package and experimental Python wrapper to internal SDK alpha channel; invite 3 beta customers to opt-in\",\n    \"Beta: widen to public SDK releases behind feature flag (enable_schema_mapper=true) and collect telemetry for coercion events\",\n    \"GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months\",\n    \"Backward compatibility: provide an adapter that maps old 'tools' flat payload to new function schema descriptors for 6 months\"\n  ],\n  \"references\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+Call+Schema+Platform+Spec\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/function-calling#streaming-handshake\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-18 Marcus Li: Initial write-up and scope. Decided to standardize on permissive coercion by default and expose strict mode.\",\n    \"2025-02-22 Elena Rodriguez: Added streaming handshake design. Concern: server needs resume_token support \\u2014 opened runtime issue #412\",\n    \"2025-02-26 Backend review (Raj Patel): Suggested adding idempotency_window header and clarified router GC implications. Marked as resolved in design notes.\",\n    \"2025-03-01 PR feedback (Sara Nguyen): Requested clearer examples for exactly-once vs at-least-once and a sample using external DB side effects. Assigned follow-up test task.\",\n    \"2025-03-05 Elena Rodriguez: Merged TS reference + Python wrappers into internal alpha branch. Triggered internal validation job; performance within budget on p3-standard test harness\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_pr\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/89\"\n  ],\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    \"design/fn-schema-mapper-v1.md\",\n    \"examples/py/function_call_echo.py\",\n    \"examples/ts/function_call_streaming.ts\",\n    \"examples/go/function_call_idempotent.go\",\n    \"benchmarks/schema-validator-overhead.csv\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"design_notes\",\n    \"implementation_plan\",\n    \"test_plan\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_169dca195c96410b80ff166803a50512\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- keep mapper small : generate validator code at package build - time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models - prefer permissive coercion by default ( string - > enum, numeric strings - > numbers ) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation - streaming handshake : introduce a small four - step exchange ( client _ hello - > server _ ack ( with resume _ token? ) - > client _ stream _ start - > keepalive frames ). if server _ ack includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non - side - effecting tools - idempotency token strategy : allow user - provided token",
